newsitem.title: UK: Brit Gas seen near Mobil take-or-pay deal.
newsitem.headline: Brit Gas seen near Mobil take-or-pay deal.

text.p: Stock market analysts said they believe British Gas is close to reaching another agreement on "take-or-pay" contracts with Mobil Corp, after a deal with British Petroleum was announced earlier today.
Without elaborating, British Gas said earlier that one or two more agreements could be expected.

Mobil, another major supplier to British Gas, said negotiations had been going on for some time and nothing has been settled yet. "It is difficult to say whether the fact BP has made an agreement will make a difference. They are independent discussions," a Mobil Europe spokesman said.
Besides a deal with BP, British Gas said it also struck a similar deal with its own production unit.
The unit and British Petroleum will be paid a total 293 million stg for giving British Gas relief in volumes and prices.
The sum to be paid to BP alone is expected to be some 245 million pounds.
Analysts believe BP may eventually be paid in kind rather than cash.

"Assets may be exchanged rather than cash. It is likely that BP and British Gas at some point in the future will start talking about BP perhaps taking the money in kind, perhaps a slice of Morecambe Bay," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
BP declined to elaborate on the details of the deal agreed with British Gas.
Morecambe Bay is a major British gas field off the coast of north west England.
